title: Bwlchgwyn Whitley LA766 Memorial
crew_summary: 8 killed including pilot WO1 David Rozell Roberts RCAF
memorial_type: Memorial garden with VE Day 1994 dedication
narrative: Warrant Officer First Class Roberts, a 22-year-old Canadian, was the pilot. Eight crew members were killed: Flight Sergeant William Henry Stewart, Flight Sergeant Robert Smeaton, Pilot Officer Ronald James Binham, Sergeant Cyril Edgar Aaron, Sergeant Alexander Taylor Strachan, Sergeant David Blackburn Lister, Sergeant Michael John Buckle, and Roberts himself. The youngest among the dead, Sergeant Lister, was just eighteen years old.

crew.name: David Rozell Roberts
crew.fate_detail: Killed when Whitley LA766 flew into the hillside at Gwernto Bach during a night navigation exercise.
crew.bio: WO1 Roberts was a 22-year-old Canadian serving with the RCAF.

memorial_details: A small memorial garden was created in Bwlchgwyn for VE Day 1994, located at the junction of Glascoed Road and Ruthin Road, adjacent to the village war memorial. The IWM War Memorials Register records the Bwlchgwyn memorial under reference 9044.

external_narratives.summary: History Points documents the RAF bomber crash site at Bwlchgwyn, recording how Whitley LA766 of 81 OTU crashed on the hillside at Gwernto Bach between Bwlchgwyn and Rhydtalog on the night of 11 January 1943, killing all eight crew.

external_narratives.summary: Aviation Safety Network records the accident of Armstrong Whitworth Whitley Mk V LA766 on 11 January 1943, confirming all eight crew were killed during the night navigational exercise from RAF Tilstock.
